name: Pipekit

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: BYO cluster starting price
plans.note: Starting at $799 per cluster per month (scales linearly with the number of connected clusters). Control plane only: all compute runs on the customer's own Kubernetes cluster and is billed by their cloud. SSO & RBAC, workflow/compute metrics, log streaming & storage included.

caveats: Chrome pricing: BYO cluster control plane starts $799/cluster/month; 30-day trial. Customer runs compute; Pipekit archives workflow logs, exposes UI/API and SSO/RBAC. Enterprise self-hosted/air-gapped control plane and support custom. $799 is NOT included compute hardware.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Free trial: 30 days, no credit card; Pipekit can provision a Pipekit-hosted free-trial cluster (not a VM/sandbox): default limits 200m CPU / 200Mi memory / 100Mi ephemeral storage per container unless overridden, overall CPU/memory/storage caps that 'cannot be increased', no persistent storage, activeDeadlineSeconds 3600 default, no guarantees of availability. free.* stays null/0 (trial, not credit).

Two deployment models: Pipekit Cloud (hosted control plane) and Self-Hosted (Helm, air-gap capable, requires a license key from sales; licenses expire). A separate 'Pipekit Support Service' (SLA-backed Argo maintainer support) is sold by meeting only; no price published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: they differ in where the control plane (UI, API, database) lives.
snapshot_auto.note: N/A by design: Pipekit is a managed control plane for Argo Workflows; compute runs as Argo pods on the customer's own Kubernetes cluster, so Pipekit has no machines to snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Argo Workflows     | Runs in your cluster
snapshot_on_demand.note: No machine/sandbox snapshots; only workflow retry/resubmit/restart via CLI. Any snapshotting would be the customer's cluster/storage.

harness_api.note: Pipekit ships an MCP server (`pipekit mcp`) so external AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) can drive Pipekit/Argo runs - the reverse direction; no API to run an agent harness inside a workload.

egress_allowlist.quote: Your workflows execute on your nodes, against your storage, using your service accounts and your secrets. Pipekit never has direct cluster credentials or inbound network access into your environment.
egress_allowlist.note: Egress control is whatever the customer's Kubernetes cluster provides (NetworkPolicy, cloud firewall); not a Pipekit feature.

ingress_rules.quote: Pipekit never has direct cluster credentials or inbound network access into your environment.
ingress_rules.note: Pipekit exposes no workload ports/preview URLs; ingress is the customer's cluster. Pipekit's own access control is SSO/RBAC over the control plane (default-deny namespaces), not network ingress to workloads.

secret_proxy.quote: You can store key value pairs in Pipekit and have them passed to your running workflow as environment variables.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are plaintext env vars inside the workflow container ('Key/value pairs are automatically mounted into your workflow as Environment variables'); no proxy.

volume_attach.quote: You cannot use persistent storage in the cluster.
volume_attach.note: Quote is for the Pipekit-hosted free-trial cluster. In production, PVCs/volumeClaimTemplates are standard Argo/Kubernetes on the customer's cluster and storage - not first-party Pipekit volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Minio does not have persistent storage. All artifacts are stored in memory and may be lost at any time.
volume_shared.note: No first-party shared volume; shared RWX storage would be the customer's cluster (e.g. NFS/EFS PVCs).

image_oci.note: Argo Workflow steps (which Pipekit orchestrates) run arbitrary container/OCI images on the customer's cluster.

docker_inside.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pipekit is a control plane for Argo Workflows on the customer's Kubernetes cluster; there is no Pipekit-managed 'machine' to run Docker-in-Docker inside, and docs describe no such capability.

nested_virt.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No /dev/kvm or nested-VM capability is mentioned; compute is customer-cluster Argo pods, not a Pipekit VM/sandbox.

desktop.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pipekit is a workflow-orchestration control plane, not a desktop/VM product.

browser.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

computer_use.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pipekit orchestrates data/CI pipelines, not browser automation.

captcha_solving.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

ssh.quote: The Pipekit CLI lets you interact with Pipekit services without leaving your terminal... submit Workflows, list Runs, stop a Run, restart or retry one
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Access is via CLI/API/UI against the Argo control plane; there is no Pipekit SSH into a machine (workflow pods live on the customer's own cluster).

snapshot.quote: Argo Workflows | Runs in your cluster
snapshot.note: No machine/sandbox snapshots; Pipekit has no compute of its own to snapshot (per feature_evidence.snapshot_auto/snapshot_on_demand in the card).

fork.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No machine to clone; only workflow retry/resubmit exists.

fork_running.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

pause_resume.quote: submit Workflows, list Runs, stop a Run, restart or retry one
pause_resume.note: CLI/API exposes stop/restart/retry of a Workflow run, not pause/resume of a running machine with reduced billing; there is no Pipekit-billed machine to pause.

wake_on_request.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Workflows run on demand when submitted; there is no sleeping machine that wakes on an inbound request.

persistent_disk.quote: You cannot use persistent storage in the cluster.
persistent_disk.note: Quote is for the Pipekit-hosted free-trial cluster; in general Pipekit itself provides no persistent disk for a 'machine' - any storage/PVC is the customer's own Kubernetes cluster.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Argo Workflow pods run to completion for the job; there's no idle-machine concept to auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No Pipekit-managed machine whose CPU/RAM could be live-resized; resources are set per Workflow/pod spec on the customer's cluster.

agent_harnesses.quote: The CLI also hosts the MCP Server that lets LLM clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Goose) call Pipekit on your behalf.
agent_harnesses.note: Direction is reversed: coding-agent harnesses can call INTO Pipekit via its MCP server; Pipekit does not preinstall/offer coding-agent harnesses inside a sandbox it runs.

own_agent_api.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pipekit has no own browser/computer-use/research agent product.

lang_python.quote: The Pipekit Python SDK lets you talk to the Pipekit API from Python... The SDK targets Python 3.10+.
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK for driving Pipekit/Argo Workflows.

lang_node.quote: Python SDK: Using the Pipekit Python SDK
lang_node.note: Docs advertise a Python SDK; no Node.js/JavaScript SDK is documented.

public_ipv4.quote: Pipekit never has direct cluster credentials or inbound network access into your environment.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no Pipekit-provisioned machine that would get a public IPv4; networking belongs to the customer's cluster.

inbound_https.quote: Pipekit never has direct cluster credentials or inbound network access into your environment.
inbound_https.note: Pipekit exposes no workload ports/preview URLs for running pipelines; access is via the Pipekit UI/API/CLI to the control plane, not HTTPS ingress to a workload machine.

guest_firewall.quote: Your workflows execute on your nodes, against your storage, using your service accounts and your secrets.
guest_firewall.note: Not applicable: root/VM guest firewall control would require Pipekit to own the machine's kernel, but compute runs on the customer's own Kubernetes cluster/nodes.

gpu.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pipekit is a workflow control plane; any GPU nodes would be part of the customer's own cluster, not a Pipekit-offered GPU machine.

windows.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pipekit targets Kubernetes/Argo Workflow (Linux container) pipelines; no Windows machine offering.

macos.quote: Build, run, and scale data & CI pipelines on Kubernetes with Argo.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

arm64.quote: We combine a linux/amd64 and a linux/arm64 variant of the containers as one image tag
arm64.note: Pipekit's own Agent/CLI containers ship linux/arm64 builds, and Argo Workflow pods can run on arm64 Kubernetes nodes.

max_session_h.quote: submit Workflows, list Runs, stop a Run, restart or retry one
max_session_h.note: Pipekit imposes no session-length cap itself; a Workflow run's duration is governed by the customer's own Argo/Kubernetes cluster and workflow spec (e.g. activeDeadlineSeconds), except the Pipekit-hosted free-trial cluster which defaults activeDeadlineSeconds to 3600s (1h).

isolation.quote: Your workflows execute on your nodes, against your storage, using your service accounts and your secrets. Pipekit never has direct cluster credentials or inbound network access into your environment.
isolation.note: derived: Pipekit is a bring-your-own-cluster control plane for Argo Workflows; the actual compute is a Kubernetes pod (container, shared kernel) on the customer's own cluster. Pipekit itself provides no VM/microVM isolation layer.

static_egress_ip.quote: Pipekit never has direct cluster credentials or inbound network access into your environment.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pipekit is a control-plane-only product (BYO cluster); it has no compute/network of its own to assign a fixed egress IP to.

eu_data_residency.quote: Pipekit is built so your workflow data, secrets, and compute stay in your infrastructure. The control plane brokers commands and metadata; the actual Workflow execution and your data never leave the cluster.
eu_data_residency.note: derived: because workflow execution and data never leave the customer's own Kubernetes cluster (and a fully self-hosted, air-gapped control plane is also offered), a customer can keep all machines/data within EU regions by choosing an EU-based cluster/deployment.

open_source.quote: pipekitprivate | ui | Private | Yes | ... You will require a Docker Hub account with access to the `pipekitprivate` repository to pull the private images. This will be provided to you as part of your Pipekit subscription.
open_source.note: Pipekit's control-plane images (ui, id, messenger, users, pipekit-init) are closed-source and distributed only as private Docker Hub images gated behind a paid subscription; self-hosting requires contacting sales for a license key (docs.pipekit.io/self-hosting-pipekit.md: 'To self-host Pipekit, contact us'). Only the CLI and agent binaries are publicly pullable, but no source repo is published (no OSS license found on pipekit.io or github.com/pipekit). Confirms open_source: false.
